演奏者面對半音排列的木條，以琴槌敲擊木條發聲，下方共鳴管會放大特定泛音。傳統文獻: The player faces the chromatically arranged wooden bars and strikes them with mallets, and the resonator tubes below amplify particular overtones. Traditional sources mention two small mallets, one in each hand; today the four-mallet grip is used, so that chords can be played. A beginner can first learn the arrangement of the bars and the position of the resonators, strike the basic pitches with a single mallet, and then practise holding several mallets and playing chords.

馬林巴以琴槌敲擊木條發聲，每條木條下方的共鳴管放大特定泛音。其音域較木琴低，音條: The marimba sounds when its wooden bars are struck with mallets, and a resonator tube below each bar amplifies particular overtones. Its range is lower than that of the xylophone, and the bars are usually arranged chromatically, like piano keys. As an idiophone, the sound is produced by the vibration of the wooden bars and modified by the resonator tubes; the details of volume control are not recorded.
馬林巴可獨奏，也見於管弦樂團、行進管樂隊的前場打擊群、打擊樂合奏、銅管與管樂隊及: The marimba can be played solo and also appears in orchestras, in the front percussion group of marching bands, in percussion ensembles, in brass and wind bands and in traditional ensembles. In Latin America it accompanies festivals, dance and religious ritual; in the United States it was also used early on in vaudeville theatre and comedy shows. Twentieth-century classical works such as Creston's Concertino for Marimba and Orchestra, Milhaud's Concerto for Marimba and Vibraphone, and works by Janáček, Orff, Henze, Boulez and Reich are all examples worth hearing.
馬林巴是體鳴打擊樂器，Hornbostel–Sachs 編號 111.212。其: The marimba is an idiophone percussion instrument, Hornbostel–Sachs number 111.212. Its wooden bars are arranged in a keyboard layout and struck with mallets, and below each bar is a resonator tube that amplifies particular overtones. Its range is lower than that of the xylophone, and the bars are usually arranged chromatically. The modern marimba can be a solo instrument and is also used in orchestras, at the front of marching bands, in percussion ensembles, in brass and concert wind bands and in other traditional ensembles.
馬林巴的早期形態見於撒哈拉以南非洲，與安哥拉、剛果民主共和國樂器相近。十六世紀隨: The early form of the marimba is found in sub-Saharan Africa, close to instruments of Angola and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It reached the Americas with Africans in the sixteenth century; there is a document from Chiapas in Mexico in 1545, and a record from Guatemala in 1680. In 1892 Corazón de Jesús Borras Moreno added a chromatic row, forming the double-row marimba; the Pacific coast of Colombia and Ecuador has kept African-descended traditions, and American makers later replaced the resonators with metal tubes, taking the instrument into orchestras and solo performance.
馬林巴的發聲體為木製音條，傳統文獻提到紅木條，瓜地馬拉雙排琴則以霍米戈木製成。共: The sounding body of the marimba is its wooden bars; traditional sources mention rosewood bars, and the Guatemalan double-row instrument uses hormigo wood. The resonators were originally, or traditionally, gourds, and later wooden resonator boxes; modern orchestral versions use metal resonator tubes tuned with metal discs. The source does not fully state the materials of the frame and the stand, though wooden components are mentioned; early Mexican sources also describe the bars threaded on cord and glued with resin, and a buzzing device used with them; the beater is a small stick whose head is coated in black wax. The materials of the rest are not stated.
